result.idea: Build an online exam-prep course for a legally-mandated certification exam (mid-size, weak-incumbent niche)

assumptions_checked.claim: Legally-mandated, non-optional, low-churn demand
assumptions_checked.evidence: FAA Part 107 is legally required to fly commercially; ~67,576 took the sUAS test in 2024 (84.2% pass), ~64,507 certs 2023, ~490K total remote pilots 2025. Mandated exams produce a steady annual inflow of new candidates. Caveat: demand is new-entrants-only (buy once), so revenue = annual new-cohort volume, not cumulative population. Source: FAA UAS testing statistics via drone-industry aggregators.

assumptions_checked.claim: 85%+ gross margin
assumptions_checked.evidence: Gross margin at 85%+ is real (trivial digital COGS). But the pitch conflates gross with net: the dominant real cost is customer acquisition (ads on high-competition exam keywords, SEO/YouTube) plus content refresh. Net/owner margin is far below 85%. True but practically irrelevant to profit.

assumptions_checked.claim: $5-25K/mo once ranked
assumptions_checked.evidence: Arithmetically plausible (67K takers x few % x ~$200-300). But 'once ranked' is the whole game and is exactly what incumbents already own. This is the winner's outcome, not the median; median new course in a niche with an entrenched incumbent makes near zero. Platform earnings-distribution reports (Teachable/Podia) were unretrievable this session (404s), so median distribution is UNVERIFIED but industry-known survivorship bias applies (project LEARNING #2).

assumptions_checked.claim: Near-passive after a 3-6mo build
assumptions_checked.evidence: Content is passive; the business is not. Ongoing non-delegable work: SEO cadence, YouTube, ad optimization, exam-change updates, student Q&A, publishing pass-rate proof, defending rank vs incumbents who outspend you. Pilot Institute runs a 29-person team. 'Passive' is the info-product marketing story, not the reality.

assumptions_checked.claim: <$30K capital
assumptions_checked.evidence: Bounded and accurate; course build + $1-2K test ads fits well under $30K. No inventory, no debt, no personal guarantee. The idea's strongest attribute; downside capped at lost time + a few $K.

assumptions_checked.claim: Proof: Drone Launch Academy ~$50K/mo on FAA Part 107
assumptions_checked.evidence: $50K/mo is a real founder claim (David Young) but dates to ~2016-2018 early-mover window right after Part 107 launched (Aug 2016) with almost no competitors; also included drone-insurance revenue, not pure course sales. Third-party estimators (AllBiz $64K/yr, RocketReach $200K) do NOT corroborate sustained $50K/mo today. Primary interview unretrievable (404s). Most damning: the niche is now closed - Pilot Institute (145K+ students, ~$1M rev, 29 staff, refund guarantee) and Drone Pilot Ground School (85K+ trained, $299) dominate. Outlier + stale + unrepresentative.

assumptions_checked.claim: A mid-size mandated exam with rising volume AND weak/dated incumbents exists (the key open question)
assumptions_checked.evidence: Every founder-adjacent candidate probed already had a strong entrenched specialist: insurance (Kaplan/ExamFX/AD Banker), EPA 608 (ESCO/Mainstream, low price), NABCEP (SEI/HeatSpring, small), ham radio (free HamStudy dominates), pilot (Sporty's/King/Gleim). No large + rising + weak-incumbent niche found. This is the make-or-break assumption and it is unsupported - matches project LEARNING 'always check for entrenched incumbents.'

competitors: Pilot Institute (FAA Part 107 + pilot): 145,647+ students, ~$1M revenue with 29-person team in 2024 (GetLatka), founded 2018, 99.9%-pass + full-refund marketing
Drone Pilot Ground School / UAV Coach: 85,000+ pilots trained, $299 individual / $249 group, $750/team Test Prep Plus upsell
Drone Launch Academy (the pitch's proof): early-mover ~$50K/mo claim from 2016-18, also sells drone insurance; current third-party rev estimates $64K-$200K/yr
Insurance licensing: Kaplan, ExamFX, AD Banker - national, decades-entrenched
EPA 608 (HVAC): ESCO Institute, Mainstream Engineering (epatest.com) - dominant, cheap, much prep quasi-free
NABCEP (solar PV): Solar Energy International (SEI), HeatSpring - recognized specialists
Pilot (private/instrument): Sporty's, King Schools, Gleim - heavyweight incumbents
Ham radio: HamStudy (free), ARRL, Ham Radio Prep - strong free option caps pricing
result.economics_verified: Capital $10-30K (pitch correct, arguably conservative). Gross margin 85%+ TRUE but net margin gutted by ad/SEO CAC + content refresh (pitch misleadingly quotes gross as if it were owner profit). Revenue: median outcome $0-3K/mo, NOT $5-25K/mo; the $5-25K/mo is a top-decile 'if you win the ranking war' outcome (the changed number - pitch omits that 'once ranked' is the whole game). Time: 15-20 hrs/wk ONGOING (content/ads/SEO/refresh), NOT passive after build (the biggest changed claim). Ramp: 3-6mo build PLUS 12-24mo distribution grind to reach rank/revenue (pitch omits the distribution timeline). Downside: low, capped at build spend, no debt/PG - holds.
kill_risks: No weak-incumbent niche actually exists - the load-bearing assumption; every viable mandated exam is already owned by a focused specialist
Distribution grind (SEO/YouTube/ads vs entrenched specialists, 12-24mo) is Hooman's single documented weakness per TRACKB_REPORT section 5 - this idea routes INTO it, not around it
Survivorship bias in the proof: $50K/mo is one 2016 early-mover outlier, partly insurance not courses, in a now-closed niche; median outcome near-zero
Generic founder-fit / no moat: 'any smart generalist can build it' means anyone can clone it; his AI/infra edge is irrelevant
Exam-change risk: certifying body can revise the exam, forcing costly refresh and invalidating rank/reviews
Free or employer-provided alternatives (ham radio, much EPA 608) cap willingness-to-pay in otherwise-plausible niches
Opportunity cost: opens a SECOND 0-to-1 distribution front while CutLog is still in its own 0-to-1 grind - the exact trap the master report warns against
result.best_niche_or_target: No verified 'large + rising + weak-incumbent' niche exists - that assumption failed validation. Least-bad framing if pursued anyway: a narrow, genuinely technical mandated exam adjacent to his EE/RF/wireless/cloud skills where he can produce visibly better technical content than a generalist incumbent (e.g., a specific RF/wireless/networking operator certification), accepting a small $3-8K/mo ceiling and the distribution grind. But do NOT pick a niche until primary data (annual test-taker count from the certifying body + audit of top-3 incumbent quality/spend) proves a real gap - that validation IS the entire first bet. Explicitly avoid Part 107, insurance, pilot, PMP/CPA (all saturated).

result.idea: Vertical bookkeeping / financial-ops subscription — pick one industry, get QuickBooks ProAdvisor certified, land 10-20 clients at $500-1,000/mo, systematize the monthly close, and delegate execution to trained bookkeepers/VAs while keeping a day job.

assumptions_checked.claim: Boringest / safest / most durable business
assumptions_checked.evidence: Demand is genuinely durable and non-cyclical (every business needs books). But 'safe' collides with heavy commoditization (thousands of local firms + offshore floor at $8-20/hr + venture players $99-599/mo) and active AI compression of the exact task being sold. Durable as a category, not obviously safe/defensible as a unit. Bench pricing bench.co/pricing (live); Pilot pilot.com/pricing (live).

assumptions_checked.claim: Fully delegable to trained bookkeepers/VAs
assumptions_checked.evidence: The LABOR (categorization/reconciliation/close) delegates cleanly — Bench/Pilot/Bookkeeper360 do it at scale (Bench had ~650 employees). But SALES, QA/review (a bad close misstates taxes = trust+liability event), and retention do NOT delegate early, and delegation costs 35-60% of revenue. Wikipedia Bench timeline (live).

assumptions_checked.claim: $5-15K/mo with 10-20 clients
assumptions_checked.evidence: Revenue math holds: at verified $300-1,500/mo/client, 10-20 clients = ~$5-20K/mo GROSS. But pitch reads it as PROFIT. After delegated labor + software + E&O + CAC, net at 15 clients (~$10.5K gross) is ~$4.5-8K/mo, not $10-15K. Top of range is best-case (20+ retained + cheap offshore + zero ongoing CAC). Vendor pricing pages (live).

assumptions_checked.claim: <$50K capital
assumptions_checked.evidence: Near-zero hard capital: QBO Accountant is free to ProAdvisors, add-ons in low $100s/mo, labor payable from client cash. Many firms start for <$5K; the $25-50K is a runway/marketing buffer, not required outlay. This is the idea's single best attribute. quickbooks.intuit.com/accountants/training-certification (live).

assumptions_checked.claim: QuickBooks ProAdvisor cert = a weekend
assumptions_checked.evidence: The QBO ProAdvisor cert is FREE, self-paced, with annual recert — passable in a weekend of study (quickbooks.intuit.com/accountants/training-certification, live). But the cert is a software-proficiency badge, NOT competence to run client books. Real competence (accrual, sales-tax nexus, payroll, trust accounting, vertical rules) takes months and is where trust-killing errors happen. The badge was never the barrier.

assumptions_checked.claim: Bookkeeping-as-a-service is a safe, proven, high-margin model
assumptions_checked.evidence: Bench raised $100M+ (through a $60M Series C, Bain/Altos/Contour/iNovia), reached ~650 employees, and still imploded overnight Dec 27 2024 — bankruptcy Jan 2025 with $65.4M liabilities vs $2.8M cash, then fire-sold to Employer.com. $100M+ of smart money could not make the model durably profitable. Wikipedia Bench Accounting (live) + TechCrunch Dec 2024.

competitors: Bench — DTC SMB bookkeeping; $199/399/599/mo + $55/hr option; raised $100M+; shut down Dec 27 2024 ($65.4M liabilities, ~650 staff), acquired by Employer.com Dec 30 2024
Pilot — startup/SMB bookkeeping+tax; Essentials $99/mo, Core custom; ships 'instant AI answers'; backed by Sequoia/Index/Stripe/Bezos, ~$100M+ raised at ~$1.2B valuation
Bookkeeper360 — multi-vertical (ecommerce/SaaS/healthcare/real estate); Monthly $399/mo, Weekly $599/mo, onboarding from $1,000; proprietary dashboard
Bookkeeper.law — law-firm vertical; $2,327/mo full-time or $14/hr
Accounting Atelier — attorneys; solo $600-800/mo, small firms $1,000-1,500/mo
Firm Balance — attorney/multi-attorney bookkeeping
Remote Books Online — lawyer vertical $300-900/mo; general SMB
MBS Accountancy — dental CPA + monthly bookkeeping (dental is a saturated 'dental CPA' niche)
Offshore/commodity floor — Fiverr/Upwork freelancers + Philippines/India BPOs at ~$8-20/hr; plus Xendoo, Bookkeeper.com, 1-800Accountant, and thousands of local firms
result.economics_verified: Price per client VERIFIED at $300-1,500/mo (horizontal $199-599; niche law/dental/ecommerce $500-1,500). Realistic steady-state P&L at 15 clients @ ~$700/mo = ~$10.5K/mo GROSS; minus delegated labor (offshore ~$75/client ≈ $1,125), software ($300-600), E&O+misc ($200-400), and amortized CAC during growth ($500-1,500) → NET ~$4.5-8K/mo at maturity, ~$4.5-6K/mo if delegated to US labor or still spending on growth. CHANGED vs pitch: the '$5-15K/mo' was read as profit but is really gross; realistic profit is ~$4.5-8K/mo (only the LOW end of the pitch is right; $12-15K is best-case, not expected). Capital CONFIRMED <$50K (actually can be <$10K) — the strongest attribute. Ramp: the pitch omits a 12-24 month personal SALES grind to fill 15-20 retained seats, in Hooman's scarce hours, plus baseline churn to out-run.
kill_risks: Sales/distribution gate is Hooman's KNOWN weakness: 0→15 clients is a 12-24mo personal sales grind competing directly with CutLog for his scarce best hours — Track-B report §5 explicitly warns against opening a second front that needs him to personally grind sales. Nearly disqualifying for a SECONDARY stream.

Thin moat + commoditization: offshore floor at $8-20/hr, venture players at $99-599/mo, thousands of local firms. Bench raised $100M+ and still died — the category's economics are a caution, not a green light.

AI/automation compression: incumbents (Pilot 'instant AI answers', Intuit/QuickBooks Live) are actively productizing AI to shrink the billable close; BLS treats the occupation as declining (~-5% 2023-33, flagged UNVERIFIED live). The service sold is the exact thing AI is eating — arguably INSIDE the AI-hype arena the mandate says to avoid.
Trust/liability delegation trap: one bad close that misstates taxes loses a client and invites claims; owner must own QA for a long time, so it is NOT hands-off early. E&O insurance mandatory.
Profit < pitch: net ~$4.5-8K/mo at 15 clients, not $10-15K; top of range is best-case only.
Low founder-fit / not his domain: real competence is months of learning (payroll, sales-tax nexus, trust accounting), not a weekend cert.
result.best_niche_or_target: Bookkeeping + financial-ops for small SaaS / indie-software / digital-product businesses (Stripe/Paddle/App-Store revenue, deferred-revenue recognition, MRR/ARR reporting, multi-currency, R&D expense tracking). Rationale: Hooman natively understands these businesses and metrics; the pain (rev-rec, Stripe reconciliation, MRR reporting) is under-served by generalist bookkeepers; it overlaps his CutLog/indie-hacker network for distribution; and it justifies premium pricing ($800-1,500/mo) + advisory upsell. AVOID the obvious saturated verticals (dental, law/trust-accounting, general ecommerce, restaurants, real estate) — all already owned by entrenched niche firms. Caveat: even this best niche only improves win-rate/pricing; it does not change the thin-moat, sales-gated, delegation-compresses-margin shape.

result.idea: Managed technical hosting / DevOps-lite subscription (HostiFi model): pick one popular self-hosted tool with a large non-technical install base, build provisioning + monitoring + billing automation, sell flat $10-50/mo/instance recurring.

assumptions_checked.claim: Reilly Chase bootstrapped HostiFi solo to $100K/yr then ~$1M ARR (then acquired/exited).
assumptions_checked.evidence: Revenue path VERIFIED and understated: HostiFi hit $10K MRR (~$120K ARR) in ~8 months of a 2019 bootstrapped launch, reached $1M ARR ~1yr early (~2021), now does $3M+/yr (some sources $7M+) with 3,000+ customers. Founder was non-technical at start, sold his house to fund it, no TinySeed funding (absent from tinyseed.com/portfolio) = bootstrapped confirmed. BUT the 'exited/acquired' framing is FALSE: Chase is still CEO and HostiFi is the acquirer (acquired SimpleFly Tech). Sources: hostifi.com, ownerpreneur.com, theorg.com/org/hostifi, crunchbase.com/organization/hostifi, hostifi.com/simplefly.

assumptions_checked.claim: Infra IS the product = 1:1 fit with Hooman's Adobe cloud/infra skills.
assumptions_checked.evidence: The actual work (provisioning DO VMs, Zabbix monitoring, Backblaze/DO Spaces backups, Let's Encrypt SSL, migrations across 32 DCs) is exactly cloud/infra/systems work, so the BUILD fit is real (hostifi.com features). BUT HostiFi's founder was NON-technical; growth came from early community position + sales/support, i.e. Hooman's flagged distribution weakness. The fit is on the wrong axis: the infra was never the bottleneck.

assumptions_checked.claim: Most AI-safe / boring / low-competition.
assumptions_checked.evidence: AI-safe TRUE (uptime/hosting isn't LLM-disintermediated). Low-competition FALSE: a horizontal 'managed self-hosted app' layer already exists and is racing pricing down — Elestio (400+ apps, from $11/mo), PikaPods (from $1.80/mo), Cloudron (EUR15-25/mo), Sliplane, plus DO/AWS 1-click marketplaces. Sources: elest.io/pricing, pikapods.com, cloudron.io/pricing.

assumptions_checked.claim: $5-25K/mo profit realistic.
assumptions_checked.evidence: HostiFi proves the ceiling exists but as a 6+yr outlier with a team. For a part-time solo operator in yr 1-2, netting $5K/mo needs ~100-300 paid instances at $19-99/mo after cloud COGS and churn — a real sales grind in a fragmented base. Realistic base case discounted to $2-8K/mo in 12-24mo; $10-25K is a multi-year outcome.

assumptions_checked.claim: ~$25-60K capital, largely bootstrappable from client cash.
assumptions_checked.evidence: No inventory/debt/PG; capital is cloud float + tooling + some ads. HostiFi literally bootstrapped from client cash. If anything <$25K is achievable, so the number improves in the idea's favor.

assumptions_checked.claim: Lowest downside in the set.
assumptions_checked.evidence: Worst case = lost time + a few $K infra spend. No inventory/debt/personal-guarantee. Consistent with master report section 5.

assumptions_checked.claim: Open question: which self-hosted tool has a large non-technical base AND does NOT compete with the vendor's own cloud? / Risk of vendor launching own cloud.
assumptions_checked.evidence: The clean niche barely exists. UniFi (best-proven) is double-covered: HostiFi incumbency PLUS Ubiquiti's OWN 'Official UniFi Hosting'/Site Manager launched ~2022 (help.ui.com article 4415364143511) — the exact vendor-cloud risk, already materialized. n8n is license-gated (Sustainable Use License limits use to 'own internal business purposes', distribution only 'free of charge for non-commercial purposes'; commercial hosting needs a separate n8n license) AND has n8n Cloud. Ghost/WordPress saturated/vendor-owned. Remaining OSS tools skew developer (technical base, breaks thesis) or hobbyist (PikaPods $1.80/mo floor). Untaken niches have NO proof point.

competitors: HostiFi — incumbent, $19/$99/$249/mo tiers (25/250/1000 devices), 3,000+ customers, $3M+/yr (some sources $7M+), bootstrapped, owns UniFi/UISP/Omada community
Ubiquiti Official UniFi Hosting / Site Manager — the VENDOR's own managed cloud, low-cost/near-free per site, launched ~2022, structural competitor to any UniFi host
Elestio (elest.io) — 400+ managed open-source apps (n8n, Supabase, Keycloak, Postgres), from $11/mo + $0.15/GB, L2 support $50/L3 $200, multi-cloud
PikaPods (pikapods.com) — resource-priced from $1.80/mo, hosts n8n/Immich/Actual; the price floor
Cloudron (cloudron.io) — self-hosting platform, Free (2 apps)/Pro EUR15/Max EUR25 per month
Sliplane, Coolify-as-a-service, DigitalOcean & AWS 1-click marketplaces — additional low-cost commoditizers of one-click OSS deploy
n8n Cloud — first-party managed hosting for n8n, disqualifying n8n as a third-party target
result.economics_verified: Capital IMPROVED vs pitch: realistically <$25K (vs pitched $25-60K), bootstrappable from client cash, no debt/inventory/PG. Margin ~60-80% after real cloud COGS (VMs, Backblaze/DO Spaces backups, Zabbix) — high, confirmed. Revenue HALVED vs pitch: realistic $2-8K/mo in 12-24mo (vs pitched $5-25K); $5K/mo needs ~100-300 paid instances; $10-25K/mo is a multi-year outlier. Ramp is SLOW — the bottleneck is community/sales grind, not the build. Downside confirmed lowest in the set (time + a few $K). Net: capital/downside better than pitched; income and ramp worse; and the moat is distribution/community, not infra — inverting the founder-fit story.
kill_risks: Vendor launches (or already runs) its own managed cloud — CONFIRMED for UniFi (~2022) and n8n; this is the base rate for any successful self-hosted tool, not a tail risk
License prohibits commercial reselling — n8n's Sustainable Use License blocks hosting-as-a-service without a paid commercial license; many modern OSS tools (SSPL/BSL/fair-source) do the same
No proven niche left — the untaken targets have NO proof point, so the #1 Track-B filter (proven playbook) fails exactly where competition is low
Distribution/community grind is Hooman's flagged weakness AND a second 0->1 front competing with CutLog for his scarce ~10-20 hrs/wk — the exact trap master report section 5 warns against
Horizontal price floor already set at $1.80-$11/mo by funded incumbents (PikaPods, Elestio), below the pitch's $10-50 assumption
24/7 uptime/on-call obligation makes it not cleanly part-time unless a contractor is hired early, which thins margin
result.best_niche_or_target: There is NO clean best target as pitched. The best-PROVEN niche (Ubiquiti UniFi/UISP/Omada network controllers, large non-technical SMB/MSP/WISP base) is disqualified for a newcomer: double-covered by incumbent HostiFi AND Ubiquiti's own Official UniFi Hosting since ~2022. The next-obvious (n8n) is license-gated + has n8n Cloud. The only CONDITIONAL path is a specific niche B2B self-hosted tool with (a) a real non-technical PAYING base, (b) no first-party cloud, and (c) a permissive license — but no such target currently has a proof point, which is why it fails the Track-B 'proven playbook' bar. Practical recommendation: do not build this from scratch; if pursuing the shape at all, validate a specific under-covered niche tool's paid demand BEFORE building, and prefer deploying capital into a cash-flowing acquisition over opening a second distribution front against CutLog.

result.idea: License an engineered product design for royalties (the Stephen Key / inventRight model): invent simple high-volume consumer-product improvements, file cheap provisional patents, build sell sheets, cold-pitch manufacturers, collect ~5% royalties — as a low-cost, no-inventory, no-personal-guarantee secondary income stream.

assumptions_checked.claim: <$5K per idea to test (provisional patent + sell sheet + prototype), no inventory, no personal guarantee
assumptions_checked.evidence: Stephen Key (the model's authority) puts it far lower: ~$100 provisional + ~$80 sell sheet = '$200 to see if your idea has legs.' Licensing means the OEM bears production/inventory/liability, so downside is capped at the per-idea spend. tim.blog/2007/11/27/how-to-rent-your-ideas-to-fortune-500-companies-part-ii/

assumptions_checked.claim: Monetizes an engineer's native output (product design)
assumptions_checked.evidence: Design is an engineer's output, but the actual work is prior-art scanning, sell-sheet copy, cold-pitching '5 or 8 or 10+' companies per idea, and negotiation. Key steers inventors toward SIMPLE high-volume products, not deep-tech. The moat is persistence/volume of pitches — exactly the fragmented-buyer distribution weakness the Track-B report flags as Hooman's gap. Not his EE/AI strength.

assumptions_checked.claim: Royalty ~5%, modest advances
assumptions_checked.evidence: Key: 'a 5% royalty is most common for consumer goods. I usually ask for 7% and settle on 5%,' on WHOLESALE (~half of retail, so ~2.5% of retail). Corroborated: UpCounsel 3-6% of wholesale; MarketBlast 3-10% for consumer goods. tim.blog 2007.

assumptions_checked.claim: $5-15K/mo across a portfolio after 18-36 months
assumptions_checked.evidence: Survivorship-biased top-of-distribution outcome, not a base case. At 5% of wholesale, $10K/mo needs a product doing ~$4.8M/yr retail — a hit. Key's own cautionary example: a product that DID license earned only '~$6,000 annually.' His success anchors (Teddy Ruxpin $1M/mo) are lottery tops he cites to contrast. Getting to $5-15K/mo reliably needs a genuine hit; realistic ramp is 3-5 yrs or never.

assumptions_checked.claim: Base rate of getting a product licensed via cold outreach is workable
assumptions_checked.evidence: No clean public conversion rate; inventRight avoids stating one ('numbers game'). Nolo: 'Chance of licensing success is low... a struggle unless you have a connection.' Key's own protocol (pitch 5-10+ companies per idea, generate many ideas, expect most to die) is itself an admission the per-idea hit rate is low (<~10%); the model works by volume of shots, not hit rate.

assumptions_checked.claim: inventRight itself: is it a coaching-upsell scheme?
assumptions_checked.evidence: Not a classic invention-promotion scam (its free YouTube content is legitimately useful), but it IS a paid-coaching funnel: Coaching $3,495 / Gateway $6,999 / APEX $17,999 (inventright.com). Reviews 3.3/5 (~14 reviews); critics call it a 'money-grab,' cite $300/hr and pressure to buy more ('if I bought more books... they would help me'). The '<$5K/idea' pitch omits $3.5K-$18K tuition. You do NOT need to pay — the method is in Key's book.

assumptions_checked.claim: Proof example: Lonnie Johnson / Super Soaker
assumptions_checked.evidence: Real but a misleading outlier: NASA/JPL engineer, product hit $200M/yr and ~$1B cumulative, and he had to SUE Hasbro, winning ~$73M in 2013 arbitration for underpaid royalties. A billion-dollar megahit + litigation is the opposite of representative. en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lonnie_Johnson_(inventor)

assumptions_checked.claim: Proof example: Rotimatic
assumptions_checked.evidence: Not a licensing story at all. Founders built Zimplistic (Singapore, 2008) and raised $16M-$42.5M of VC across ~5 rounds (Tracxn $16M; TheCompanyCheck $42.5M from Credence/EDBI/Openspace). It is the exact VC-funded hardware path the royalty model is meant to AVOID. Citing it as proof is simply wrong.

competitors: inventRight (Stephen Key & Andrew Krauss) — dominant coaching brand, 25+ yrs, 10M+ YouTube views, programs $3,495 / $6,999 / $17,999
MarketBlast — inventor-to-manufacturer submission marketplace (~1,500+ companies looking for ideas)
Edison Nation / Inventors Launchpad ecosystem — submission/aggregator platforms that gate access and take a cut
OEM open-innovation portals (Spin Master, Hasbro, P&G Connect+Develop) — the actual buyers, inundated, default to 'no'; they own the channel
Long tail of invention-promotion scam firms (USPTO-warned) — charge thousands to 'evaluate' and deliver nothing; poison trust for cold outreach
result.economics_verified: Cost per idea: $200-$1,000 out of pocket (cheaper than the '<$5K' pitch), BUT add $0 (DIY) to $3.5K-$18K if you buy inventRight coaching. Royalty: 5% of wholesale ≈ 2.5% of retail (verified, on the smaller base). Per-idea odds of licensing: <~10%, a volume game (dozens of ideas to land a few deals). Typical licensed-product income: $0-$6K/YR each (Key's own drum-key example), not $5-15K/mo. To net $10K/mo needs one product doing ~$4.8M/yr retail — a hit. Downside: genuinely low, capped at a few $K + time (VERIFIED). BIGGEST CHANGE vs pitch: the '$5-15K/mo after 18-36mo' income claim — reframed as a near-free lottery ticket that MIGHT compound over 3-5+ yrs, not a reliable income engine. Also both cited proofs collapse (Rotimatic is VC-funded, Johnson is an outlier who had to sue for $73M).
kill_risks: Survivorship-biased income: base case is $0-low-thousands/yr per idea; $5-15K/mo requires a genuine hit most inventors never get
It's a sales/persistence game, not an engineering game — hits Hooman's documented weakness (cold outreach to fragmented buyers) and does NOT leverage his EE/AI strength
Time competes directly with CutLog for the same scarce evening hours — unlike a buy-and-operate asset that consumes capital + delegation
Royalty enforcement risk: even megahits get shorted (Lonnie Johnson sued Hasbro for $73M); auditing/collecting from OEMs is ongoing adversarial work
Coaching-upsell temptation: easy to sink $3.5K-$18K into inventRight chasing the dream; paid-tier ROI unproven (3.3/5, 'money-grab' complaints)
Aggregators/OEMs own the deal-flow channel — you're one of thousands in the submission pile, no moat
Both cited proofs are broken (Rotimatic is VC-funded not licensed; Johnson is an outlier + lawsuit) — a red flag about the underlying thesis
result.best_niche_or_target: Simple, high-unit-volume consumer-product IMPROVEMENTS (not deep-tech, not from-scratch inventions) in an un-sexy, fragmented category with many mid-size OEMs running open-submission programs — e.g. workshop/tools, EDC, pet, kitchen gadgets, or home-organization. Pitch via a one-page sell sheet + provisional patent to 8-15 manufacturers through MarketBlast plus direct OEM open-submission portals. Avoid toys (Spin Master/Hasbro gatekeeping + trend risk) and anything needing regulatory approval or custom manufacturing. Run it DIY from Key's book (skip paid coaching), as a near-zero-cost background bet with zero income expectation — never stealing hours from CutLog.

result.idea: Buy a cash-flowing boring B2B / vertical micro-SaaS ($2-8K MRR, $80-150K all-cash) and operate/improve it as a secondary income stream
